questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'. **

My sisters-in-law (1)/who lives in Kolkata (2)/have come to stay with us. (3)/No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence has an error in the second part. 
 
• From the context of the sentence, it can be easily interpreted that the statement is for many people. 
 
• Hence, **'lives'** should be changed to** 'live' **as **“sisters-in-law” **are living in Kolkata which is **plural.**
 
• Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *My sisters-in-law who **live **in Kolkata have come to stay with us.*

**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

The employee did not _____ to the argument of the manager.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Concede**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer for the given blank is "**concede**".
 
• The word "**concede**" means **to admit or acknowledge the truth of something, often unwillingly.**
 
• In the given sentence, the employee did not agree with the argument of the manager.
 
• Therefore, the correct word to fill in the blank is "**concede**".
 
 
• *Example: He finally **conceded **that he had made a mistake.*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other words and their meanings are:
 
• **Precede **- to come before something or someone in order or time
 
 
• Example: The opening speech will **precede **the awards ceremony.
 
 
 
• **Exceed** - to be greater than a particular number or amount
 
 
• Example: The cost of the project **exceeded **our budget.
 
 
 
• **Recede **- to move back or away from a previous position
 
 
• Example: The floodwaters began to **recede **after a few days.

**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. **

Nugatory
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Productive.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**nugatory**" means **of no value or importance, useless, ineffective, or futile**.
 
• Here are** example sentences:**
 
 
• The committee's decision was **nugatory **and had no impact on the final outcome.
 
• The company's efforts to improve their image proved to be **nugatory **in the face of mounting criticism.
 
 
 
• The correct answer for the opposite of "**nugatory**" is **option 4) productive,** which means **yielding good results, profitable, or useful. **
 
• **Example sentences** for "**productive**" are:
 
 
• The company's new strategy was very **productive **and led to a significant increase in revenue.
 
• She spent the weekend working on her garden, and it turned out to be very **productive **with a variety of flowers and vegetables.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other options in the question are:
 
• **Delusive**: misleading, deceptive, or illusory.
 
 
• Example: The promise of overnight wealth from the get-rich-quick scheme turned out to be **delusive**, and many people lost their savings.
 
 
 
• **Futile**: useless, ineffective, or incapable of producing any result.
 
 
• Example: His efforts to revive the dying plant were **futile**, and it eventually withered away.
 
 
 
• **Unreal**: imaginary, not real, or lacking substance.
 
 
• Example: The vivid dream felt so real, but it was actually **unreal**, and she woke up feeling disoriented.

questions.question:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".

I had (not only helped him by) giving hints but also with providing him links.

options.text: helped not only to him by

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**helped her not only by**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• When using ***not only . . . but also*** in a sentence, **parallelism**** should be the goal**. It means that the words following both parts of this correlative conjunction (i.e., *not only* and *but also*) should belong to the same parts of speech. For example, if a verb follows *not only*, then a verb should also follow *but also*. Using different parts of speech after each part of *not only . . . but also* makes the sentence imbalanced and, frankly, just awkward. 
 
• **Consider the example below:**
 
 
• He’s not only intelligent but also funny.
 
• the adjectives *intelligent* and *funny* follow *not only* and *but also*, ensuring that the sentence is parallel.
 
 
 
• ​Here, in the given sentence 'but also' is followed by preposition, so 'not only' should also be followed by preposition.

​**Thus, the correct sentence is: ***I had helped him** not only by** giving hints but also with providing him links.*

**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph. **

P: In other countries which are populated by 'haves', frustration is among them also because they do "haves". 

Q: In some countries, frustration exists because these countries are populated by "have-nots". 

R: Frustration is global cancer. 

S: It has spared no country.
questions.solution:
In such questions, The correct order should be like a story or a well-presented fact.

The correct order here is RSQP.

R presents the topic.

S gives its effect.

Q further develops the topic by taking examples.

And lastly, P tells about the other possibility to the topic.

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P: The real purpose underlying this maxim lies in its utility in the worldly sense. 

Q: He has within him a spirit which is ever exhorting him to cut down his needs and learn to be happy with what he has. 

R: Man is something much greater than an intelligent being using his intellect to make newer inventions from time to time. 

S: It tells us to be up and doing, not to be passive in our attitude to life.
questions.solution:
In such questions, The correct order should be like a story or a well-presented fact. The correct order here is RQPS. 

Here, the quality of a man is discussed. R starts the fact by making some qualities peculiar. Then Q adds on to the qualities in continuation. Then statement P continues the paragraph by developing about what was said in 2nd statement. Lastly, S completes the paragraph by mentioning the most important aspect-”life”.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

Why do you waste money?

options.text: Why is money been wasted by you?
Why has money been wasted by you?
Why is money wasted by you?
Why is money being wasted by you?

questions.solution: On transition from the given Active voice to Passive voice, the correct Passive voice is option 3. The active voice is being said in Present form of tense. Then the passive voice must follow present tense. Since, Options 2 and 4 are past forms, therefore, they are to be eliminated. Option 1 is grammatically incorrect and hence eliminated too.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech.**

The doctor said, "well, what can I do for you?"

options.text: The doctor wanted to know what he could do for her.
The doctor said that he couldn't do anything for her.
The doctor asked what he couldn't do for her.
The doctor wondered what he could do for her.

questions.solution: Generally when transitioning from direct to indirect form of speech,”that” is used. But here, ‘that’ is used in statement 2 which is incorrect and has completely changed meaning to the given direct speech. The meaning of the statement should never be changed in such transition. Similarly options 3 and 4 are also incorrect due to slight changes in meaning. The correct indirect speech would be option 1

questions.question: The world has seen a _____ growth in several spheres.

It is by common knowledge that one can easily state that there has been a lot of development and still growing. From this context the filler in the blank should be an adjective showing immense development. Since, ‘tremendous’ is the only appropriate word to be used, therefore, the correct option would be 1.

questions.question: Agricultural production, industrial production, communication, medicine, education etc, have seen _____ growth.

questions.question: We can safely assume that the future is not as _____ as once appeared to be.
questions.solution: Earlier, due to lack of scientific discoveries and evolution of science, people could not see the brighter side of the world. But now, due to the evolution of science, the future is not as bad as earlier people expected. So the correct filler would be bleak.
